input.content: Since pinned maintenance windows were added: pinned windows (Window::pinned, is_pinned) bypass the merge fold entirely — they are filtered out before the sort, appended verbatim afterwards, and the combined result is re-sorted by (start, end). Regular windows still obey the existing invariant (sorted fold, only last.end grows). Consequence: output is still sorted by start, but is pairwise non-overlapping only among regular windows — a pinned window may overlap a merged regular window, and duplicate pinned windows are all kept. Callers like first_gap that assume a fully non-overlapping schedule are only guaranteed that for pin-free input. Pinned-ness participates in PartialEq (private `pinned` field), so Window::new(2,3) != Window::pinned(2,3).

content.text:
Done. Pinned maintenance windows are implemented in `src/scheduling.rs` and all tests pass (the primary test plus the full suite: 23 tests, 3 suites).

What I changed:

- **`Window`** gained a private `pinned: bool` field. `Window::new` sets it false, the new `Window::pinned(start, end)` constructor sets it true, and `is_pinned()` exposes it. Because the field participates in the derived `PartialEq`, `Window::pinned(2, 3)` is distinct from `Window::new(2, 3)`, which the test relies on.
- **`merge_windows`** now filters pinned windows out before the sort-and-fold (so they can neither be merged nor absorb regular windows), merges regular windows exactly as before, then appends every pinned window verbatim and re-sorts the combined output by `(start, end)`.

Before touching the code I used `recall` on `merge_windows`, which surfaced an invariant: the fold only grows `last.end` and is correct only because of the `(start, end)` sort, and callers like `first_gap` expect sorted, non-overlapping output. My change preserves that for regular windows, but a pinned window can now legitimately overlap a merged regular one — so I recorded an updated invariant memory noting that the fully-non-overlapping guarantee now only holds for pin-free input.
